purpose: Source-only presentation clock/recording association and bounded CPU shader-clock archive track
sourceBehavior: The approved exact-image profile identifies the game clock helper, epoch, guard and shader call; binding checks the actual RIP-relative storage operands and E8 caller
Only public QueryPerformanceCounter/Frequency APIs are called; private epoch initialization is neither invoked nor forced
Uninitialized/initializing static guards, changed epoch/guard/frequency, invalid counters and arithmetic overflow suppress the sample
Completed client-tick marker receipts retain the sampled game presentation clock; the full owned receipt reaches Java through the existing native appearance command
Schema-2 native shader observations carry the same domain and require the total input to lie between before/after public samples
The initial world/marker association requires a common domain and a presentation difference within three seconds; its original simulation-based mappedStartTimeMs remains separate
AppearanceHistory retains the association in manifest source metadata; old source metadata and shader schema 1 remain readable without inventing a presentation mapping

ShaderClockHistory records only when the initial association is available, indexes actual native shader samples in presentation time, and preserves tick/partial/elapsed/native remainders/world phase/skip/override values
One render observation can span multiple native world passes; worldSequence distinguishes them, and an identical repeat of the same world sample is ignored
Distinct samples at equal presentation times are retained in native world order; complete equal-time groups stay in one bounded block and an excessive group explicitly fails the take
Track blocks use existing serialized bounded AppearanceHistory compression/hash/index machinery, with 64 samples per block, 8 KiB per sample and a 1 MiB raw block bound
The final exclusive descriptor end uses nextUp(last observed time), without adding or moving an observation
Loading validates source mapping/domain/session, all blocks, monotonic observation/world/tick/elapsed clocks, exact mapped point bits, compression completion/trailing bytes and the content hashes
Reader caches at most two blocks and exposes all observations at an exact presentation instant; it never interpolates or holds across missing observations
Presentation track endpoints are reported separately from the simulation appearance duration; status does not claim phase restoration or GPU/video readiness
remaining: Native replay reconstruction selecting and restoring recorded absolute/world phases at arbitrary output times
Verified mapping of packet/relay, simulation and presentation timelines, including pause and seek behavior
Complete installed-build reader/hook/layout family and material/scene owner joins
Native cosmetics phase insertion, GPU rendering and deterministic video parity
